task: Set distance (m) from 1 to 4; mass (kg) from 0.5 to 5, and read force (N), which has noise. The law has the form: force = strength mass distance^-exponent. Find strength, exponent. Then submit your claim. It is scored on settings you cannot probe.

steps.text: I start by probing the force at a fixed mass of 1 kg and a distance of 1 m. This gives a baseline for the strength. I will then vary the distance at the same mass to find the exponent, and check the mass scaling.

The data fit force = 20 * mass / d^2. At 1 kg the force is 20.0 N at 1 m, 5.007 N at 2 m and 1.257 N at 4 m, so the exponent is 2. At 4 kg and 1 m the force is 79.96 N, about 4 times 20, so force is linear in mass. The strength is about 20.0. I am submitting this claim now.
The claim was acknowledged (submitted: 1.0). I submitted strength 20.0 and exponent 2.0, and I have nothing further to run.
